name: nokkvi
description: A rust based navidrome client for linux built using iced-rs

paragraphs: A native Rust/Iced client for Navidrome music server. Named after Old Norse nökkvi, a small, humble boat.
Demo of Nokkvi's GPU-accelerated audio visualizers and how the layout adapts to different window sizes.

⚠️ AI-Generated Project This entire codebase was written by AI (primarily Claude) with my direction. I'm not a developer. I come up with the ideas, test things, and use this as my daily music player, but I don't write code myself. You'll probably find patterns in here that experienced Rust developers would do differently. If you spot something that could be better, issues and PRs are welcome.
features: Native PipeWire audio engine: gapless playback, a 10-band EQ, ReplayGain and AGC normalization, and configurable crossfade with transition fades.
Opt-in bit-perfect playback (Strict or Relaxed, follows the native sample rate) with a badge that reads the real hardware clock as BIT-PERFECT, RESAMPLED, or UNVERIFIED.

GPU visualizer with bars, lines, and scope modes plus beat glow, bloom, trails, echo, reflection, horizon, a spiralling tunnel inside the scope ring, and CRT, shown in a band above the player bar or over the cover art,…
Theater Mode (F11): the playing track's cover, visualizer, and lyrics fill the window, with an auto-hiding player bar and optional fullscreen.
Smart playlists authored in-app: a rules editor with nested All/Any groups, live validation, presets, a raw-JSON mode, and server-evaluated previews. Also imports .nsp (needs Navidrome 0.61+).
